items.text: This weekend I had the opportunity to join @lilinksinc and @ESC_NY_Links for their 2025 Family Wellness Expo. These remarkable women are committed to addressing issues affecting the African American community across Long Island and Eastern Shore, and this event was a perfect example of their dedication.

15 years ago today, the #AffordableCareAct was signed into law. 

The uninsured rate is at an all-time low, with 24M buying their own coverage & 21M on Medicaid. 133M with pre-existing conditions are protected, Rx costs cut, & premiums lowered by $2,400/year.

It is crucial to protect the Affordable Care Act to ensure continued access to healthcare for all Americans.

170,285 Nassau County residents depend on Medicaid. I will oppose any legislation that threatens to take away their coverage. https://t.co/Qv8t5nQRHo

This week I joined local health leaders to discuss how cuts to Medicaid will raise health care costs for all Americans. We should be working to bring down the outrageous cost of health care, not ripping Long Islanders away from the coverage they count on.

I’m glad that @secduffy agrees that we must improve Long Island’s dangerous roads. Too many of our community members have lost their lives to traffic accidents. This urgent crisis must end now.

The footage of Senator Alex Padilla being physically restrained and thrown to the ground today is completely shocking and unacceptable. 

This is no way to govern. The Administration must provide immediate answers and accountability for this horrifying treatment.

Slashing Medicaid will lead to higher health care costs, longer wait times and reduced services at hospitals for ALL Americans, even those with private insurance. 

We should be fighting to protect and expand access to quality, affordable health care, not making it more expensive and less accessible for everyone.

Cuts to Medicaid will destabilize our entire health care system, putting nursing homes and hospitals at risk of closing and raising health care costs, even for those with private insurance.  

I voted against this partisan bill because it’s wrong for Nassau County.

Let’s be clear: the GOP tax bill is morally bankrupt and economically reckless. It slashes Medicaid and SNAP programs that millions of our families, children, seniors and veterans rely on every day for health care and food assistance while adding trillions to the national debt. 

https://t.co/NKu7D4BrtT

The GOP tax bill will gut New York’s health care system, making it harder for people to access quality, affordable medical care and ripping health care coverage away from 1.5 million New Yorkers. 

This is indefensible. https://t.co/CirbPXesOF

The Republican tax bill includes the largest cuts to health care and food assistance in modern history. This is a direct assault on American families, seniors, and veterans—people who can least afford to pay the price.

I was proud to join my Democratic Caucus colleagues to speak out against the budget bill that punishes NY, hospitals, veterans and the most vulnerable Americans. This bill will raise costs for every American and raises our debt burden by almost $4T. It’s not beautiful it’s bad. https://t.co/uOG3qkCDWh

.@LeaderJeffries is on the House Floor sharing stories about Americans who count on Medicaid and SNAP to survive. Their lives will be devastated by these extreme cuts in this bill.

Yesterday, I heard directly from @littlelobbyists—a brave group of families advocating for their loved ones with special needs. They opened up about the incredible challenges they face and how the proposed Medicaid cuts will hurt them.

I will never stop fighting for these families who stand to lose everything if this reckless bill becomes law.

I am committed to continuing the fight to protect Medicare and Medicaid for my constituents and the American people.

Congress should be coming together to negotiate a bipartisan package that keeps the government open, restores funding for local law enforcement and preserves the tax credits that keep health insurance premium costs down. I’m calling on my GOP colleagues to choose cooperation over gridlock for the good of the American people.

We’re in the middle of a cost-of-living crisis and if Congress lets the Affordable Care Act tax credits expire, Long Islanders who rely on them would see their monthly health care premiums spike by 32%. We can’t let families get priced out of the care they need.
